discovery: Cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of primordial density perturbations
motivation: Guth proposed inflation, an early epoch of accelerated expansion that explains why the universe is flat, homogeneous and free of relics. Linde developed new and chaotic inflation, the framework in which realistic models are still built. Mukhanov, with Chibisov, showed that quantum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed all cosmic structure, and predicted a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted, adiabatic Gaussian spectrum. These predictions have since been tested with great precision. COBE, WMAP, Planck, ACT, SPT and galaxy surveys confirmed spatial flatness, adiabatic superhorizon fluctuations shown by the CMB acoustic peaks and TE anticorrelation, near-Gaussianity, and a spectral index of n_s ≈ 0.965, deviating from 1 at more than 8σ. What began as speculation about the first 10^-35 seconds is now quantitative, empirically grounded physics. It also motivates the ongoing search for primordial gravitational-wave B-modes.
